result.title: RangeRectQuant: Compressing Scientific Fields for Every Future Rectangular Sum
result.comment: 10 pages, 6 figures. Code, data, core experiments and extended figures: https://github.com/Marchematics/RangeRectQuant
result.summary: Scientific rasters are often stored before the regions to be measured are known. Independent pixel-error bounds can force exact integer reconstruction when one absolute error budget covers every future rectangle. Coordinated changes allow every pixel to change while every rectangular sum remains accurate. A prefix sum accumulates values from the top-left corner. Four such sums determine any rectangular total. RangeRectQuant preserves the pixel range and designated exact samples while controlling errors in prefix sums. At each row position, we characterize exactly which errors let the remaining pixels meet these constraints. These errors form a single integer interval, even when many completions exist. A backward pass finds its endpoints; a forward pass uses them to choose quantized pixels. The resulting field meets the prescribed error budget for every axis-aligned rectangle, with linear work and workspace proportional to one row. Experiments on geographically held-out built-surface and water-occurrence maps show substantial storage savings over alternatives meeting the same requirements. Data producers encode once; later users measure arbitrary rectangles without the source, re-encoding, or query-specific correction.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RangeRectQuant，通过前后向两遍扫描在整数区间内选取量化像素值，使保留像素范围与精确采样点的同时，任意轴对齐矩形求和都满足给定误差预算，实现科学栅格数据的线性时间压缩。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作属科学栅格数据的存储压缩与量化误差控制，围绕矩形求和预算与内存占用，未涉及视觉表征、latent 状态生成或推理决策，也未提供可直接借鉴的状态更新或监督线索。
